boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UM-Dearborn spaces documented by a 2025 university student guide for studying, collaborating, taking breaks, and spending time between classes.

cards.title: CASL Atrium
cards.subtitle: College of Arts, Sciences, and Letters
cards.notes: Use the central atrium’s varied seating and floor-to-ceiling windows for a social study session, then pause to reset between classes.
cards.short_summary: A bright, central setting for shared work or a quiet break.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn identifies the CASL atrium as a social study space with varied seating and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.access_notes: Located in the College of Arts, Sciences, and Letters building.

cards.title: Language Lab
cards.subtitle: Third level of CASL
cards.notes: Bring a partner or work independently using the computers, display equipment, projectors, charging stations, and language-tutoring resources.
cards.short_summary: A tech-equipped CASL workspace for individual or collaborative language work.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn says the Language Lab supports individual or group work and has computers, screens, projectors, charging stations, and Arabic, French, and Spanish tutors.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third level of the CASL building.

cards.entity_name: Mardigian Library First and Second Floors
cards.title: Mardigian Library First and Second Floors
cards.subtitle: Mardigian Library
cards.notes: Meet a group around the second-floor whiteboards or use its meeting rooms and computer station; take a first-floor break before returning.
cards.short_summary: Library floors that combine group-work tools with break-time amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn describes second-floor study areas with meeting rooms, a computer station, whiteboards, and movable charging stations; its first floor includes Mug Life Café and Stamelos Art Gallery.
cards.access_notes: Inside Mardigian Library; the source distinguishes the first and second floors.

cards.entity_name: Mardigian Library Third and Fourth Floors
cards.title: Mardigian Library Third and Fourth Floors
cards.subtitle: Mardigian Library
cards.notes: Choose these upper floors when your work needs a quieter setting, and settle into the desks designed for focused reading or writing.
cards.short_summary: Upper-library desks intended for concentrated, quieter work.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn characterizes the Mardigian Library’s third and fourth floors as quieter study areas with desks for focus and concentration.
cards.access_notes: Inside Mardigian Library; the source distinguishes the third and fourth floors.

cards.title: Wolverine Commons
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Renick University Center
cards.notes: Set up a solo task or bring a study group and select from the different seating arrangements in this social RUC workspace.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, social study area in the renovated university center.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn describes Wolverine Commons on the RUC’s second floor as a social study spot with varied seating for solo work or groups.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the James C. Renick University Center.

cards.title: Renick University Center Renovated Lounge
cards.subtitle: James C. Renick University Center
cards.notes: Use a couch for independent reading or take a study booth with classmates; the lounge includes updated seating and a fireplace.
cards.short_summary: An updated RUC lounge built around couches and study booths.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn reports that the renovated RUC study lounge includes couches, study booths, a fireplace, and updated seating.
cards.access_notes: Inside the James C. Renick University Center.

cards.title: Natural Science Building Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Natural Science Building, south end of campus
cards.notes: Try a different floor to find its color scheme and scenic view, then use the seating, charging stations, and whiteboards for group work.
cards.short_summary: Three floors of study areas with shared whiteboards and charging.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn says the Natural Science Building has study areas across three floors with scenic views, whiteboards, markers, charging stations, and seating.
cards.access_notes: Located at the south end of UM-Dearborn’s campus.

cards.title: Tony England Engineering Lab Building
cards.subtitle: Engineering Lab Building (ELB)
cards.notes: Meet teammates in an open study area with large windows and whiteboards, or choose an enclosed lounge space when you need less activity.
cards.short_summary: Engineering building work zones ranging from open tables to enclosed lounges.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn describes the ELB as having diverse study areas with large windows, whiteboards, accessible lighting, and more enclosed lounge spaces.
cards.access_notes: Known on campus as the Engineering Lab Building (ELB).

cards.title: RUC Patio
cards.subtitle: Behind the Renick University Center
cards.notes: On a warm day, take coursework or conversation outdoors and use the patio seating between the CASL building and university center.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor study-and-hangout area behind the RUC.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn identifies the patio behind the RUC as a warmer-month study and hangout spot with seating and access to CASL and the RUC.
cards.access_notes: Located behind the Renick University Center; suited to warmer conditions.

cards.title: Chancellor’s Pond
cards.subtitle: UM-Dearborn campus
cards.notes: Pack a book or lunch and use the stone benches or yellow chairs beside the pond; the fountain operates in spring, weather permitting.
cards.short_summary: A pond-side campus pause point with seating for reading or lunch.
cards.evidence_claim: UM-Dearborn says Chancellor’s Pond has a fountain brought to life each spring, plus yellow chairs and stone benches for lunch or reading.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; the source notes the fountain returns each spring.
